R1_output_emission.justification: each committed token requires the host to observe either the token id (4B, weak) or the full 512-expert routing scores (2048B, strong, current sampler contract)

R2_causal_cut_set.justification: 48 sequential layer boundaries; router input (2560 F32) must be complete before layer l runs; with 5 disjoint coordinate shards at least 2048B crosses a rank cut per boundary; cut-set capacity bounds completion time

R3_active_expert_dram.justification: 10/512 experts active per layer; their weights must be read once per token; L2 (128MB) covers at most 128MB of the 11.1GB per-GPU expert pool, so at least (1-128/11100) of the active set comes from DRAM; generous to implementations (assumes perfect L2 retention across randomly routed tokens)

R4_fp32_alu.justification: attention projections + router + 11 experts per layer, 48 layers; RX 6800 has no FP32 matrix cores so vector ALU peak applies; lossless representation changes bytes, not FLOPs

combination_rule: per-row lower bound = max(R1, R2, R3, R4): distinct physical resources may overlap in a legal implementation; same-resource work adds
mtp_relaxation: perfect acceptance (rows per public token >= 1); bound is per target row, so per-public-token bound equals it
